etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English investigacioun, from Old French investigacion, from Latin investigatio. Morphologically investigate +‎ -ion

definitions.definition: The act of investigating; the process of inquiring into or following up; research, especially patient or thorough inquiry or examination

quote.citation: 2015, Gregg Barak, editor, The Routledge International Handbook of the Crimes of the Powerful‎[1]:
quote.text: "Ag-gag laws criminalize undercover investigations by prohibiting one or more of three types of behavior: trespass, recording of videos, and failure to submit a video to law enforcement."

quote.citation: 2018 August 18, Michael S. Schmidt and Maggie Haberman, “White House Counsel, Don McGahn, Has Cooperated Extensively in Mueller Inquiry”, in The New York Times‎[2]:
